messages:
elena: heads-up — we got a last-minute upstream firmware advisory for the eu-west1 GPU hosts. ops plan is still to run the planned maintenance tonight but we should nudge the window 30m earlier to avoid a big customer batch job window. can @samir take the on-call handoff and confirm? :rotating_light:

infra-bot: scheduled-task queued: fw-update gpu-pool-eu-west1; maintenance_id=fw-eu-3391; earliest_start=2026-03-18T01:00:00Z; estimated_drain=~3m per node. Automated drain jobs will post once started.

samir: taking it. i can start the drain at 00:30Z instead of 01:00Z. will run a canary on 2 serving nodes first and then proceed. ping me if the customer impact list changes.

elena: thanks. main asks: (1) small statuspage blurb we can post at the start and update when complete, (2) short customer-facing email for affected dedicated customers, (3) oncall runbook snippet for the drain/rollback. keep templates concise.

katie: i can draft the customer email. which customers are "affected"? only those on dedicated eu-west pools or anyone routing through that region?

pranav: affected = customers with dedicated capacity pinned to eu-west1 OR customers with routing preference eu-west1 and recent traffic > 1000 rps in the last 24h. mike-cs pls pull the list and we'll target top 10.

samir: quick runbook snippet (will paste into ops channel when we start):
```
# drain sequence (eu-west1)
# 1) cordon node: redwoodctl node cordon <node-id>
# 2) start drain: redwoodctl drain start <node-id> --timeout 180
# 3) monitor metrics: grafana->serving/latency, kv-cache-hit-rate
# 4) if tail latency > 500ms for >2m -> abort drain and rollback: redwoodctl drain abort <node-id>
```

pranav: good. add explicit rollback message to status page: "we will roll back automatically if latency exceeds thresholds; no user data will be lost."

mike-cs: pulling customer list now, will DM the top 10 and post a short list here.

katie: customer email draft (short):
```
Subject: Planned maintenance in eu-west1 — possible brief serving interruptions
Body:
Hi <CustomerName>,
We will perform a planned maintenance on the eu-west1 inference pool on 18 Mar 2026 between 00:30–01:30 UTC. During the work we expect brief (<=3 minutes per node) serving restarts that may cause transient increased latency or very short request errors for a small fraction of requests.
What we are doing: applying a firmware update to GPU hosts.
Impact: possible 2–5 minute rolling latency blips; no data loss.
If you have a business-critical job during this window and need us to shift timing, reply and we’ll coordinate.
Thanks,
Redwood Support
```

elena: looks good. add a line offering a post-maint follow-up summary for customers who request it.

mike-cs: posting list: @katie DM sent to top10 (names redacted here). also posted a public statuspage draft below.

pranav: paste statuspage draft here so we can iterate. keep it tiny.

mike-cs: statuspage draft:
```
Status: maintenance in progress
Summary: Applying GPU host firmware update in eu-west1; rolling restarts of serving nodes.
Impact: transient increased latency and rare short errors for requests routed through eu-west1. Estimated duration: ~60 minutes for the region; brief node-level restarts ~2–3 minutes each.
Mitigation: Canary-first rollout, automatic rollback on latency threshold, targeted customer notifications sent.
Updates: will post when 50% and 100% complete.
```

elena: great — i updated the start time to 00:30Z and set oncall to samir. i'll post the statuspage at start + pin this thread. samir — shout if you need extra hands for rollback.

samir: will do. infra-bot will emit progress posts; i'll post manual updates at 50% and done. starting canary in ~10m.

infra-bot: maintenance-event fw-eu-3391: canary start on node gpu-eu-02; timestamp=2026-03-18T00:30:45Z

elena: canary looks healthy so far, latency OK on two nodes. proceeding with staged drains.

infra-bot: maintenance-event fw-eu-3391: 50% complete; nodes updated=6/12; timestamp=2026-03-18T00:47:12Z

samir: 50% update: short latency spikes seen at 00:44–00:46 for ~90s, auto-rollback thresholds not hit. continuing.

mike-cs: emailed top10 customers with the note and offered follow-up. one customer replied asking for the post-maint summary. noted.

infra-bot: maintenance-event fw-eu-3391: 100% complete; nodes updated=12/12; timestamp=2026-03-18T00:59:36Z

elena: done — rolling validation checks green, no follow-up incidents. posting final statuspage update and sending summary to customers who requested it. :white_check_mark:

samir: handing back oncall to regular rotation. all good from SRE side.

katie: final customer summary sent to requesters. thanks team.

elena: closing thread — tag repo: ops/maint-logs/fw-eu-3391 and attach metrics snapshot to the incident ticket. good job everyone.
